paris-le-de-france-escapes-chevreuse-val.slogan: A 245 km loop out of Chevreuse Valley Dawn Loop
paris-le-de-france-escapes-chevreuse-val.story: A proper escape from Paris with roads worth waking up for. Out of Villiers-le-Bel and back again: 245 km, roughly 5 h 07 in the saddle. The stops in between: Scenic stretch in Mitry-Mory, in Mennecy and Rungis. The climb of the day is near Ozoir-la-Ferrière. The line favours views over speed.

paris-le-de-france-escapes-chevreuse-val.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: This Scenic stretch in Mitry-Mory → High point near Ozoir-la-Ferrière stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Photo stop in Mennecy → Rungis is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

Food stop near Les Essarts-le-Roi → Vigny, on the way back can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.
